The short version for Morgan Park homeowners

Most houses around Morgan Park went up in the 1950s. Housing that age normally still has its original trim, and that trim is already carrying a lot of paint. It is the reason two painters can look at the same Morgan Park house and hand you very different numbers. One of them has priced the preparation and one of them has not.

In Morgan Park that mostly means exterior painting and interior painting, with drywall repair on the same visit often enough that splitting them wastes everyone's time. We are 8.0 straight-line miles away at 7900 W. 83rd St. in Bridgeview.

  • Can we do your job? Almost certainly. In Morgan Park it is exterior painting and interior painting most weeks, plus the drywall, plaster and carpentry that goes underneath both.
  • What will it cost? There is no price list on this site, because there is no honest local one to publish yet. Every job is quoted after we walk it. What moves the number on a Morgan Park house is how much has already been painted onto the trim, because taking that back is most of the labor on a Morgan Park interior.
  • What usually needs doing first? The prep, almost always. On housing this age in Morgan Park the ceilings and the woodwork decide the job, and both of them come before the first finish coat.
  • When can you come? We are 8.0 straight-line miles out, and travel is not a hidden line on a quote from us. Straightforwardly, for most jobs. Morgan Park is in the middle ring, so a walk-through costs nothing but a visit and the date comes off the call.

What we look at before we price the work

On stock with a 1953 median, the interior quote is decided by trim footage and not by wall area. 6.6 rooms is a lot of door casing, window casing and baseboard for the square footage, and every run of it is already carrying decades of paint. Original casing with sixty years on it prices very differently from casing that was stripped or replaced, which is the first thing worth establishing before anybody gives you a number. With 6,047 owner households and 2,430 renting, this is two markets in one place: owners doing a room or an elevation at a time, and small landlords wanting a unit turned around cleanly between tenants. They are not the same quote.

What an estimate here has to account for

  • Distance, stated. Morgan Park is 8.0 straight-line miles from the shop. Travel to Morgan Park is not a hidden line item on this site and it should not be one on a written quote either.
  • Containment, not just paint. 83.4 percent of housing in Morgan Park was built before 1970, so on most addresses here the lead-safe setup and the cleanup are part of the job and part of the hours.
  • Plaster as well as drywall. 28.2 percent of Morgan Park is prewar. Plaster cracks along the lath and comes back if it is only filled, so wall repair is a different line from wall painting.
  • Trim, counted separately. At a median of 6.6 rooms, casing, baseboard and doors are the half of an interior that actually varies. A single number for the whole house hides it.

What the housing here is likely made of

Most of it is postwar brick: bungalow, Cape Cod and the first generation of ranch. Little of the outside takes paint at all, so a Morgan Park exterior is soffit, fascia, overhangs, doors and the garage. Inside it is small rooms with a great deal of casing in them.

Two figures produce that sentence and no others: build year 1953, and a stock that is 75 percent detached, 4.6 percent attached and 20.4 percent in buildings of two or more.

Read it as a starting assumption rather than a finding. No public dataset records what the walls in Morgan Park are made from, so attaching a number to it would mean inventing one. The house itself answers faster than any table can.

Old paint in Morgan Park, and how it has to be handled

Assume there is old paint under the current coat. On 1950s housing, which is most of Morgan Park, that is the safe assumption, and paint from before 1978 can be leaded. It affects the setup of a Morgan Park job at both ends, the sealing off before and the cleanup after, and not much in between.

The practical content of it is dust. Where paint in a Morgan Park room gets disturbed past about six square feet, twenty outside, or wherever a window comes out, the work has to be contained and cleaned to a standard. That is time at both ends of the job, and it is why an honest quote on 6,047 homes worth of 1953-median housing reads longer than a fast one.

None of it is graded at the town line. The rule attaches to a build year and to the work being done, so the number worth checking is the one on your own deed in Morgan Park.

83.4 percent of housing units were built before 1970, and the community-area data does not publish a 1978 bucket, so the real pre-1978 share is higher than that by an amount nobody has measured in Morgan Park. Stock of that age brings the federal lead-safe renovation rule with it. The rule turns on two things, a build year before 1978 and work that disturbs the paint, and in Illinois EPA enforces it directly instead of a state program doing it.

Ask about it early. It changes the sequence of a job rather than the price of the paint, and a contractor who has thought about it will tell you in plain terms what happens on day one.

This site does not claim EPA lead-safe firm certification. No number has been supplied, so the trust panel below shows it as pending. Ask for it directly, from anyone quoting work in Morgan Park.

Of the 8,987 housing units in Morgan Park, 83.4 percent were built before 1970 and 28.2 percent before 1940, against a median build year of 1953. This is old-city housing, and it behaves like it: plaster, deep casing and a lot of coats already on the woodwork.

Morgan Park is 71.3 percent owner occupied, 6,047 households against 2,430 renting. 20.4 percent of units are in buildings of two or more, 4.6 percent are attached, and the remaining 75 percent are detached houses averaging 6.6 rooms. Median home value is $247,659.

Against the other 22 Chicago community areas covered here, Morgan Park sits in the top four for the largest homes by room count (6.6 rooms).

Three figures put Morgan Park a long way from the average of the 76 places on this site: prewar housing at 28.2 percent against a 15.8 percent average, housing built before 1970 at 83.4 percent against a 56.9 percent average and townhomes and rowhouses at 4.6 percent against a 7.5 percent average.

Source: Chicago Metropolitan Agency for Planning, Community Data Snapshots 2026, drawing on American Community Survey 2024 estimates. Every dollar figure on this page is a published Census estimate of what homes in the area are worth. None of it is a price for work.

Who actually shows up in Morgan Park?

Mike Walsh owns the company, walks the job and stays on it while our crew works. Call 708-935-4289. It is worth saying because on a job this size the gap between whoever measured it and whoever turns up is where most of the disappointment comes from.

Can it be done a room at a time?

Yes. With a median of 6.6 rooms in Morgan Park a full interior is a real commitment, and there is nothing wrong with taking it in pieces. The one thing worth planning is the order, so that the rooms that get used most are not the ones sitting under plastic in December.

What changes the price most on a house here?

The state of the trim and the ceilings. Wall area is predictable, and with 6.6 median rooms and a 1953 median build year in Morgan Park the woodwork is where the hours actually go. Ask for it as its own line and the differences between two quotes stop being mysterious.
